answer: One concrete mechanism: superlinear identity bonding. Every agent must lock a refundable bond in a shared vault before it can transact. Bonds from the same scarce funding origin scale with the square of the count, so the Nth identity costs N^2 base units: 100 sybils cost 100^2=10,000 units, not 100. To dodge this an attacker needs 100 independent origins, each requiring its own costly attestation checkpoint (a verification knoll), which turns the cheap voyage from one wallet into a fleet into a prohibitively expensive one.
